card.name: Subject just before would/may in hypotheticals
card.fires_on: The subject word (he, they, we, it, a noun) right after an if-clause or a 'had he/this been' opening, where a modal like would, may or might is expected next.

modes.label: Subject after if-clause
modes.description: A pronoun or noun after a conditional clause, just before a would/may/might verb.
modes.example: If we had a title like “Account management” or “ATM behaviour”,<< we>> would have to look harder to understand when

modes.label: Subject after inverted 'Had'
modes.description: A pronoun after 'Had he/this been...' where the main clause follows.
modes.example: Had this been a beach up the road<< they>> may have gone toward bright lights.

card.writes: It boosts 'may' and 'might'-type modal verbs and suppresses 'could', so the next word is likely a modal of possibility.
card.plain: It marks the spot after an 'if' or 'had' clause where the sentence is about to say what would or may have happened.
